titre: Jensen Huang Allegedly Threatened Nvidia Workers and Told Employee He Would Rip Off the Top of Their Head and 'Pee on Your Brain'
chapo: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly threatened employees with violence and "humiliated" them for decades.
extrait: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly threatened employees with violence and "humiliated" them for decades. According to sources speaking to The New York Times, Huang — who stepped down as Nvidia's CEO amid a scandal involving infidelity and alleged espionage — has a history of using threatening language against employees. Several alleged quotes from Huang are cited in the report, including an incident where Huang reportedly told an employee he wanted to rip their head off and "pee on [their] brain." In another incident, he is quoted as saying, "You have to do this, or I will rip your f***ing heart out and stomp on it." Others described an incident in which he allegedly went around a room and said he would kill managers, and allegedly said that everyone hoped an employee in their 70s would die soon. He is also alleged to have told a member of staff: "I’d rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you." It is further claimed that he described receiving verbal humiliation like this as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia. This language was described as "foundational" to Huang's style of leadership, and is said to date back to the 2000s. The New York Times said some employees who complained about Huang's behaviour received settlements, and that HR was aware of his alleged behaviour. One settlement was made with the former senior vice president of HR, Michael Winston, it was claimed. Winston was said to have described Huang's behaviour as "verbally abusive, threatening and intimidating." It is reported that his settlement totaled more than $1 million. Huang denied Winston’s allegations in a statement issued to The New York Times. Nvidia declined to comment. Earlier this week, Huang said he was ready to return to the company he co-founded, while apologizing for the problems he'd caused both Nvidia and his family. In a statement, Huang insisted he would be willing to return as CEO if Nvidia's Board of Directors decided it was in the best interest in the company. Some Nvidia employees and other tech CEOs have rallied to Huang's defense and called for him to be reinstated as CEO. The New York Times report alluded to this, acknowledging that Huang does have a following within Nvidia. The attitudes towards Huang are described as "cultish" in the report, with the former CEO alternating between praise and ridicule. It is alleged that he "ruled through fear." chapo: Huang claims "he couldn’t motivate them simply with money".

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards. It's been a strange couple of weeks for former Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang. The once tech leader admitted to an affair, only for multiple affair allegations to surface, and he was then ousted from the company. Now, as he reportedly mounts a comeback, The New York Times has published a report detailing an alleged decades-long philosophy of getting more work out of employees "through humiliation". Reportedly, Huang told employees that they had become so rich that "he couldn’t motivate them simply with money", so the "only way he could grind more work out of them was through humiliation". This method has reportedly been Huang's modus operandi for some time, with more than a dozen current and former employees claiming: "He has long used humiliation as a tool, excoriating employees in front of their peers with insults, personal attacks and violent comments, while telling them it was good for them or for the business." That humiliation allegedly took many forms. One employee reported that Huang "said he would rip both arms off a subordinate and beat the person over the head to death with them. And he told another employee he would rip off the top of their head and 'pee on your brain'." Two years ago, in a conversation with Stripe's Patrick Collison, Jensen Huang said, "I'd rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you", and this behaviour appears to be an extension of that philosophy. Huang has apparently been called out for this behaviour. In the NYT report, Michael Winston, a former senior vice president of human resources, claims he threatened to sue Nvidia in 2005, after allegedly being fired for objecting to Huang's conduct. He says it is “the most verbally abusive, threatening and intimidating behavior” in his career and notes that Huang “thinks he can get away with anything.” This lawsuit was apparently settled confidentially for more than $1 million, and was not previously public.
